references.text: The Lord says he will harden Pharaoh's heart, the same theme as in 4:21 about God strengthening Pharaoh's heart so that he does not let the people go.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened and he did not listen to Moses and Aaron, fulfilling what the Lord said in 4:21.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart so that he did not listen to them, a repetition of the theme from 4:21.
The Lord says he has hardened Pharaoh's heart and the hearts of his servants to show his signs, parallel to 4:21.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart so that he would not let the Israelites go, a direct fulfillment of 4:21.
Moses and Aaron performed all these wonders before Pharaoh, but the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, summarizing the theme from 4:21.
The Lord says he will harden Pharaoh's heart so that he pursues the Israelites, a continuation of the theme from 4:21.
The Lord hardened Sihon's spirit and made his heart unyielding, the same divine action as with Pharaoh in Exodus 4:21.
The Lord hardened the hearts of the Canaanite people so that they went to war against Israel, the same principle as with Pharaoh in Exodus 4:21.
God commands Isaiah to harden the people's heart, a parallel theme on divine hardening as in Exodus 4:21.
Paul quotes the story of Pharaoh and discusses how God hardens whom he wills, a direct reference to Exodus 4:21.
John quotes Isaiah that God has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, the same theological theme as in Exodus 4:21.
It illuminates the connection between God's hardening of Pharaoh and the subsequent 'strong hand' that frees the people.
It complements the prophecy of hardening with the final phase where Pharaoh himself drives the people out.
It confirms the fulfillment of the prophecy of hardening given in 4:21.
